issue.title: Add a --shout option to greet and document it in docs/
issue.problem: bin/greet.js has no --shout option. Any argument starting with `--` is silently dropped, so `node bin/greet.js --shout Ann` prints `Hello, Ann!` and exits 0, which is the same as running it without the flag. docs/index.md, which the pages workflow (.github/workflows/pages.yml) publishes to https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ on every push to main, documents only `node bin/greet.js <name>` and mentions no options.
issue.reason: Support wants a louder greeting for the lobby screen, and they need a docs page they can send people to that describes it. Right now the flag looks like it works but does nothing, and the docs don't mention it.
issue.outcome: `greet --shout <name>` prints the greeting in upper case. Plain `greet <name>` behaves as before. docs/index.md describes --shout, so the next deploy from main publishes it on the docs site.
expect: `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` prints exactly `HELLO, ADA!` followed by a newline on stdout and exits 0.
`node bin/greet.js Ada --shout` (flag after the name) prints exactly `HELLO, ADA!` followed by a newline and exits 0.
`node bin/greet.js Ada` (no flag) still prints exactly `Hello, Ada!` followed by a newline and exits 0.
`node bin/greet.js --shout` with no name still writes `usage: greet <name>` (or a usage line that names the --shout option) to stderr, prints nothing to stdout, and exits 2.
docs/index.md documents the --shout option: it names `--shout`, shows a usage example, and says that the greeting is printed in upper case (for example `HELLO, <NAME>!`).
`npm test` passes and includes at least one test that runs the CLI with --shout and checks the upper-case output.

non_goals: Checking that the live site https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ shows the change. That only happens after merge, when the existing pages workflow deploys docs/ from main. This issue only needs docs/index.md updated in the PR.
Changing the pages workflow or how the docs are published.
Adding other options (short `-s` alias, custom punctuation, colors) or an argument-parsing library.
Publishing a new npm version or changing the package version.
assumptions: 'Louder' means the whole greeting is printed in upper case, so `Hello, Ada!` becomes `HELLO, ADA!` with the same punctuation.
--shout works whether it comes before or after the name, because the current CLI already accepts `--` arguments in any position.
'Shows up on the published docs site' is met by updating docs/index.md. The README says that directory is published on every push to main, so the PR can't check the live site itself.
Missing-name behaviour stays the same: a usage message on stderr and exit code 2.
